en: Paeon just asked you, again, whether it may restart the same container, for the same alert.
You said Go, again.
Could it stop asking?
Observe records what would have been done.
Suggest tells you, with no button.
Approve waits for your Go.
Auto runs, verifies, then tells you.
The default is suggest.
A level is set per alert, per action and per container.
That is one policy line, in your rules file.
Every run you approve is recorded: verified, failed, undone, or, this was wrong.
After five approved, verified runs in a row, of the same action, on the same container, for the same alert, Paeon shows the policy line that would let it run alone.
It proposes. Adding the line is your commit.
Auto never applies to an incident with several alert classes, under the confidence threshold, or twice on one incident.
One failed verification, one Undo, or one, this was wrong, takes it back.
The action asks for your approval again, until you reinstate it, next to the executor.
The kill switch is a button on every result notification, a button in the console, a command, or an environment variable.
Everything drops to observe.
Only you can resume, next to the executor.
Autonomy is earned, per action and per container.
And it is yours to take back.
